title: Voice agents with Realtime Video — Sidney Primas, LemonSlice
talk_summary: Sidney Primas of LemonSlice describes building real-time photorealistic video avatars: a video diffusion transformer made interactive via causal attention masking, distilled from ~30 denoising steps to one, plus a custom fix for long-horizon error accumulation and heavy CPU/GPU streaming orchestration. The transferable parts are about long-running streaming pipelines, error compounding over long runs, and treating orchestration/harness engineering as core value.

takeaways.technique: Treat the harness/orchestration layer as the product, not glue
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly say most of their productizing value is in 'model hardness' (harness): orchestrating many threads, GPU vs CPU work, queues, buffering, interrupts so the stream never stutters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I feel like a lot of our value actually in like productizing this is in the model hardness.

takeaways.what_they_do: They identify that each generated block carries error, and feeding past output back as context compounds it over hours; they built a dedicated mechanism (undisclosed) to keep long continuous runs stable without resets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each video block you generate has some error in it... you're looking at the error, you're adding more error to it, and then just the error compounds over time
takeaways.numbers: Avatars run 8-16 hours continuously with no reset

takeaways.what_they_do: They retrain with an attention mask so the model can only attend to the past, because at inference the future doesn't exist yet; this forces the architecture to match deployment reality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we basically train a model with an attention mask so that the model can only look into the past

takeaways.technique: Distill many-step process to one step
takeaways.what_they_do: They compress a 30-step denoising loop into a single step to hit real-time latency and cost parity with a much lighter modality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we need to do is go from like 30 steps, bring it out to one step
takeaways.numbers: ~30 denoising steps reduced to 1; cost roughly equal to a voice model

takeaways.technique: Build your own task-specific benchmark before you can pass it
takeaways.what_they_do: They are constructing their own avatar Turing test with real people, planning to publish it and track progress over time even though they won't pass it this year.
